US.extension: B-1/B-2 visitors already in the United States may apply to extend their stay with USCIS on Form I-539, filed online or by mail before the I-94 admit-until date expires — USCIS suggests filing at least 45 days before expiry. Fee per the USCIS Fee Schedule (Form G-1055, edition 26 October 2026): $420 online / $470 on paper, with no separate biometrics fee. Extensions are granted in increments of up to 6 months. VWP (ESTA) travellers generally cannot extend their stay or change status.
US.overstay: There is no published overstay fine schedule. Staying past the I-94 admit-until date leaves you out of status: under INA 222(g) your visa is automatically voided, and unlawful presence accrues — more than 180 days but less than 1 year in a single stay triggers a 3-year bar on re-admission once you depart, and 1 year or more triggers a 10-year bar (INA 212(a)(9)(B)). The bars apply when you leave and again seek admission. Filing Form I-539 before the stay expires is the recognised way to avoid accruing unlawful presence while USCIS decides the request.

IN.extension: The official e-Visa terms state that an e-Visa is non-extendable and non-convertible — plan to leave within the stay granted. IN.overstay: The official e-Visa pages publish no penalty table for overstaying, so no fixed fine figure is quoted here. Overstaying is an offence under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025: you must regularise your stay through the e-FRRO portal and obtain an exit permit before you can leave, and any penalty is assessed on your case. Overstaying can also count against future visa applications.

FR.extension: A short-stay visa cannot be extended as a rule. Under Article 33 of the Visa Code, it may be extended only on proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing departure (free of charge), or for serious personal reasons (a fee of €30 applies). The authority that decides is that of the Member State where you are present — in France, the préfecture of the place where you are staying.
FR.overstay: No official overstay tariff is published in the sources used here. Staying beyond the 90 days in any 180-day period, or beyond your visa, makes the stay illegal: under the Return Directive (2008/115/EC) the Member State must issue a return decision, which may be accompanied by an entry ban for the whole Schengen area, set case by case and normally no longer than five years.

documents: A passport valid for the trip
Check the France-Visas wizard before you travel to confirm your nationality is visa-exempt for your purpose of stay

routes.notes: France applies the Schengen-wide rule: the 90 days are shared across all Schengen states, so days spent in any other Schengen country count against the same 90-day allowance.

routes.stay: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen area, not per country.
routes.who: Nationals of the countries in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 — including the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Brazil, Mexico and the EU/EEA states. Find your passport in the status table below.

Passport, valid for at least 3 months after your planned departure from the Schengen area, issued within the last 10 years, with at least 2 blank pages
France-Visas application form, completed online, printed and signed, with the receipt
Photo meeting ICAO standards
Travel medical insurance covering emergency care, hospitalisation and repatriation for the whole Schengen area and the full stay
Supporting documents for the purpose of the stay, means of subsistence, accommodation and intention to return, as the wizard lists for your case
Fingerprints are collected when you lodge the application (exemptions exist for specific categories)

The fee, time limits and document rules are set at EU level and are the same for every Schengen state.
routes.processing: Decided within 15 calendar days of lodging an admissible application (Visa Code, Article 23), extendable to a maximum of 45 calendar days where further scrutiny is needed. Apply no earlier than 6 months and no later than 15 days before travel.
routes.stay: Up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area. The visa is valid for the whole Schengen area.
routes.who: Nationals of the countries in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 — everyone who is not visa-exempt for France. France issues the uniform Schengen short-stay visa (type C) under the EU Visa Code, so the fee, time limits and document framework below are the Schengen-wide standard, not a France-only rule. TH.extension: The Immigration Bureau charges THB 1,900 per extension application (form TM.7, with a 4 x 6 cm photograph). A visa-exempt entry for tourism can be extended once, by up to 30 days, under clause 2.4 of Immigration Bureau Order No. 327/2557; the extra days run from the day the current permission ends. Apply in person at an immigration office before the current stay expires.
TH.overstay: The Immigration Bureau (Division 1 FAQ) states the fine for overstaying is THB 500 per day, up to a maximum of THB 20,000. Overstaying can also bring detention, deportation and a re-entry ban under Ministry of Interior Order No. 1/2558, with the length depending on the overstay period and whether the traveller surrenders or is arrested.

Onward travel ticket within 30 days
Proof of funds if asked (Thai embassies cite THB 10,000-20,000 per person)

Mauritius and Seychelles get a separate 15-day exemption. All foreign nationals must also submit the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) at tdac.immigration.go.th within 3 days before arrival. Land-border entries under the exemption are generally limited to twice per calendar year.

AU.extension: There is no visa extension product. Home Affairs states: "You must apply for a new visa if you want to stay longer in Australia." A new Visitor visa (subclass 600, Tourist stream) can be applied for from inside Australia (AUD 630) before the current visa expires, but only if the current visa does not carry a No Further Stay condition (8503, 8534, 8535 or 8540); if it does, a waiver must be sought first (Form 1447). From 28 November 2026 condition 8503 becomes mandatory on visitor visas applied for on or after that date, so onshore re-application will generally no longer be possible for those holders.
AU.overstay: Home Affairs publishes no overstay fine schedule. Staying in Australia without a valid visa is unlawful: the person cannot work, attend school or access Medicare, and may be detained and removed by the Australian Border Force and billed for the cost of removal. A person who leaves after being without a valid visa for more than 28 days may be refused another visa for up to 3 years, except in limited circumstances. Anyone whose visa has expired should contact the Immigration Status Resolution Service or apply for a Bridging visa E to arrange departure.

documents: Valid New Zealand passport
Completed incoming passenger card
Meet health and character requirements
routes.fee: No fee. The SCV is granted on arrival at no charge.
routes.name: Visa-free entry
routes.notes: Under the 1973 Trans-Tasman Travel Arrangement. SCV holders may live, work and study in Australia. From 1 July 2023, eligible SCV holders can apply directly for Australian citizenship by conferral after meeting residence requirements. New Zealand permanent residents travelling on another country's passport do not qualify.
routes.processing: Granted on arrival at the airport or seaport. No application before travel.
routes.stay: Indefinite while the Special Category visa (subclass 444) is in effect. The SCV is granted on arrival, ceases on departure, and a new SCV is granted on each re-entry. It is a temporary visa, not permanent residence.
routes.who: New Zealand citizens holding a valid New Zealand passport only. No other passport qualifies: all other passport holders need a visa before travelling to Australia.

documents: Valid eligible passport
ETA (601): application lodged only via the Australian ETA app; eVisitor (651): application lodged online via ImmiAccount
Payment method for the AUD 20 ETA service charge (card, Apple Pay or Google Pay); no payment for the eVisitor
Must be outside Australia when applying and when the visa is decided
routes.fee: ETA (601): no visa application charge; an AUD 20 service charge applies for use of the Australian ETA app. eVisitor (651): free — no visa application charge and no service charge.
routes.name: ETA (subclass 601) / eVisitor (subclass 651)
routes.notes: For tourism or business visitor activities only; no work, and study or training up to 3 months only. From 28 November 2026, condition 8503 (No Further Stay) becomes mandatory for ETA and eVisitor applications made on or after that date (Migration Amendment (Preventing Further Stay for Visitor Visas) Regulations 2026, F2026L01503): the holder cannot be granted most other substantive visas while in Australia, other than a protection visa, unless the condition is waived. Visas already granted are not affected.
routes.processing: 50% and 90% of recently decided ETA (601) and eVisitor (651) applications were finalised in under 1 day (Home Affairs global visa processing times, published 2 November 2026, for applications finalised to 30 September 2026). A guide only, not a commitment; most ETA decisions are given immediately in the app.
routes.stay: Up to 3 months per visit; multiple entries within a 12-month validity period, or until the passport expires, whichever is sooner.
routes.who: ETA (subclass 601): holders of ETA-eligible passports from 34 countries and jurisdictions. ETA-only passports, i.e. not eligible for the free eVisitor, are Brunei, Canada, Hong Kong (SAR of China), Japan, Malaysia, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan (excluding official or diplomatic passports), the United States, and British National (Overseas) passports. eVisitor (subclass 651): holders of eligible European passports from 36 countries — the EU member states plus Andorra, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Norway, San Marino, Switzerland, the United Kingdom (British Citizen only) and Vatican City. European passport holders who qualify for both should use the free eVisitor instead of the ETA. Non-citizen passports and certificates of identity are not eligible for either.

documents: Valid passport
Itemised personal bank statements for a 3-month period, plus pay slips, audited accounts, tax records, term deposits or credit card statements as applicable

Evidence of a genuine temporary visit: travel plans, an invitation letter from a relative or friend in Australia if applicable, and reasons to return home (employer letter, proof of study, immediate family at home, or property and other major assets)
Proof of enough money for the stay and to leave Australia; Home Affairs publishes no minimum bank balance
Apply online through ImmiAccount; for the offshore Tourist stream the applicant must be outside Australia when applying and when the decision is made
routes.fee: Tourist stream: AUD 250 per applicant when applying outside Australia; AUD 630 when applying in Australia. Sponsored Family, Business Visitor and Approved Destination Status streams: AUD 250. Frequent Traveller stream: AUD 1,845. Charges in force from 1 July 2026. A subsequent temporary application charge of AUD 700 can apply to onshore applications depending on visa history. Charges are not refunded on refusal.
routes.name: Visitor visa (subclass 600)
routes.notes: No work; study or training up to 3 months only. From 28 November 2026, condition 8503 (No Further Stay) is mandatory for Visitor visa applications made on or after that date (F2026L01503): the holder cannot be granted most other substantive visas while in Australia, other than a protection visa, unless the condition is waived. Visas already granted are not affected.
routes.processing: Tourist stream (Home Affairs global visa processing times, published 2 November 2026, for applications finalised to 30 September 2026): 50% decided within 21 days, 90% within 31 days. These are percentiles of recently decided applications — a guide only, not a commitment or service standard.
routes.stay: Tourist stream: generally 3 months, up to 12 months in certain circumstances, decided case by case. Parents of Australian citizens or permanent residents may be granted validity over 12 months but cannot stay more than 12 months in total in any 18-month period. Frequent Traveller stream: up to 3 months per visit, visa valid up to 10 years, with no more than 12 months in Australia in total in any 24-month period.
routes.who: All other passport holders, including nationals not eligible for an ETA or eVisitor, and ETA/eVisitor-eligible travellers who need a stay longer than 3 months per visit or have a criminal conviction or other complicating factor. Tourist stream (outside Australia) is the standard route. The Frequent Traveller stream is only for passport holders of China, Brunei, Cambodia, the Philippines, Laos, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam and Timor-Leste (11 countries).
